question_text: [Caching Strategies, Invalidation & Idempotency - Q45] How does Probabilistic Early Expiration (XFetch algorithm) prevent a Cache Stampede when a high-traffic cache key expires?

options.text: By permanently locking the database table
By computing an exponential probability that a random client will recompute and refresh the cache *before* it officially expires, based on delta compute time and remaining TTL
By serving HTTP 503 errors to all clients during expiration

answer_explanation: XFetch evaluates `-beta * delta * ln(random()) > remaining_ttl`. As expiration approaches, probability increases that a single worker will refresh the key in the background, preventing stampedes.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: XFetch evaluates `-beta * delta * ln(random()) > remaining_ttl`. As expiration approaches, probability increases that a single worker will refresh the key in the background, preventing stampedes.

criteria.description: Selects the exact correct technical option.
